shot1: The first shot fades in from black, using a medium-to-wide shot at eye level inside the tunnel beneath the stands. The subject stands slightly right of center, with the distant end of the background faintly revealing the cool morning light of the stadium. Depth of field is moderate to ensure both the person and the practice sword are clearly visible. Soft natural light enters from the side of the tunnel, preserving realistic shadow layers on the face and wrists, while occasional side light creates brief glints along the edge of the sword. Her sleeve and hair strands show slight movement. The starting motion is controlled, with muscle force transmitted sequentially through the shoulder, elbow, and wrist.
shot2: The second shot cuts abruptly from the previous one to the trackside, using a low-angle, eye-level tracking shot that transitions from wide to medium. The red curved track and grass edge form horizontal leading lines. The subject enters from the left side of the frame, with the background showing the empty morning stands and sky not yet fully bright. The space is more open, allowing full release of the action’s explosive power. Lighting remains primarily natural, but side lighting more distinctly outlines the blade and outer arm contours, clearly capturing the movement of the hem and footfalls. She first steps forward to complete the advance, then performs cloud hands with the sword, rotating her wrist in a circular motion, drawing a smooth arc along the outer side of her body axis. Next, she spins and slashes downward, lowering her center of gravity and tapping the ground at the lowest point to leverage momentum, then quickly taps again and flicks upward. The kinetic chain transfers from ankle, knee, hip, through the shoulder and arm to the sword tip—explosive yet controlled. The hem and ends of her hair swing naturally with the spin, showing delayed motion. The camera initially tracks horizontally to keep her centered, then makes a small circular movement during the spin, tilts slightly down during the slash to follow the blade's descent, and quickly pulls back to a medium shot during the flick-up, enhancing speed and spatial displacement. The overall atmosphere remains quiet and concentrated.
shot3: The third shot transitions from the previous one via a brief fade-in/fade-out, shifting naturally to the central open area of the stadium. It uses a combination of close-up and extreme close-up shots at eye level with a slight upward angle. The subject is centered in the frame, with a small amount of blurred ground texture in the foreground and an open field with soft morning light in the background. The composition is tighter, with focus firmly locked on her upper body, sword-holding hand, and the tip of the blade. The overall tone remains neutral, with natural light as the base, supplemented by a subtle rim light from the side-rear to clean up the silhouette of the stopped blade and facial outline. Continuing the momentum from the previous shot, she lifts her knee and completes her form, bringing the sword-hand steadily back to a controlled position. The blade tip initially trembles slightly due to inertia, then gradually comes to rest. Her shoulders and back sink again, her gaze fixes forward, and she transitions from post-explosion tension to an inwardly gathered state, completing the closing of the motion. The camera first pulls back slightly to show her full retraction, then slowly pushes in to a close-up where the blade tip and eyes are both sharply in focus, capturing the final moment of stabilization.
